notes: Modified cash basis village; governmental = General, Street, Fire and Ambulance and Other Governmental funds (Total Governmental Funds column, pp5-6); business-type = Water and Sewer (p8 Total column, modified cash basis; disbursements equal p2 business-type expenditures 113,763 and charges 178,060). Roll-forward on fund balance: 424,597 + 601,503 - 563,440 + 76,449 - 76,449 = 462,660; transfers are fund-column sums (Total column blank). Business-type: 437,790 + 178,570 - 113,763 = 502,597 (measure cash as FY2023: net position = cash, p1 and p7 both 502,597). Ending cash = cash and cash equivalents + cash at county treasurer (p4); no investments printed; no beginning cash printed. County treasurer revenues 218,983 split using the Statement of Activities general revenues (p3: property taxes 169,436, motor vehicle taxes 14,507, both equal to the p11 county treasurer schedule); remainder 35,040 kept as taxes (p11 shows it is homestead, prorate, in-lieu, carline, interest and state tax credit less collection fees, i.e. mixed types; it does not tie to p3 Intergovernmental sources, which is 1,000 higher because p3 shows street operating grants 88,340 vs highway allocation 89,340). p2 functions differ from p5 by 1-2 dollars of rounding (GG 147,697 vs 147,695, public safety 56,696 vs 56,697, streets 77,112 vs 77,113; same total 563,440). Water Fund other revenue 467 is shown on p3 as a general revenue, not in charges for services, so category other. Balance sheet: governmental lines from the governmental funds statement (p4, totals equal p1 462,660); business-type from p1. Detail: the budget schedule (p9) is a combined all-funds schedule (not recorded), so per-fund statement columns are used for General, Street, Fire and Ambulance (pp5-6), Water and Sewer (p8); nonmajor funds per fund column of their combining schedule (p10, 9 funds). p10 prints Trash Fund spending 45,869 on the General government row (p5 shows it as Trash). County Treasurer schedule (p11) not recorded in detail: the same money is in the County treasurer revenues lines. Read pages 1-11 of 11
